images.title: Varga, ghana and mula
images.purpose: Shows the old Indian words for a square, a cube and a root: varga, ghana and mula, the root of a plant.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Three items in one row, evenly spaced, each with a picture and two short words under it.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 3 items in one horizontal row. Item 1: a flat square filled teal (#0072B2), with varga and square under it. Item 2: a cube in flat oblique view filled amber (#E69F00), with ghana and cube under it. Item 3: a small sprout with two leaves outlined dark above a short ground line, and its branching root below the line drawn in reddish purple (#CC79A7), with mula and root under it. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A square root was named after the root of a plant, the thing a square grows from.
images.description: Shows the old Indian words for a square, a cube and a root: varga, ghana and mula, the root of a plant.
images.context: Varga is the square, ghana the cube, mula the root; via Arabic jidhr and Latin radix to root.

image_decisions.why: Three named pictures carry the history of the words without crowding the frame.
